facade.name: Barraka restaurant: parapet, clerestory windows, door, glazed awnings and thatched edge
facade.trust: Wall height: on IMG_2618 the parapet is about 2.4 times the black door. Taking the door as 2.05 m gives a wall of about 4.9 m; the model uses 4.8 m. The 2014-15 laser survey records this roof at a median of 2.89 m and a high point of 3.67 m (docs/reviews/lidar-levels, 6364501UF1366S_part8), below the photographed parapet. That survey figure is kept as the roof deck or an older roof, not as a reason to squash the clerestory into the registry's 3 m storey. The ring is not moved. North-east openings are read from the square-on IMG_2618 (pin +-2.4 m, camera not solved): two groups of three brown-framed windows, not the three groups of three the task brief counted; IMG_2615 is the same wall seen obliquely. The door is under the landward group. The louvred vent sits in the parapet between the groups; the small slot vent below the timber band is the second vent in IMG_2615 and its station is the less certain of the two. South-west: IMG_2604 shows eight clerestory windows, two red scalloped awnings, glazing, frosted BARRAKA BEACH lettering, a thatched eaves and a rooftop tank. North-west: IMG_2630 and IMG_2611 show glazing and one awning on the west corner, then a plain wall with one small window. Stations along the walls are estimates of about a metre. Lettering, scallops and the tank are simplified. Not built: the cooking shelter, net mound and kayaks (IMG_2619), the slot drains (IMG_2610, IMG_2630, IMG_2631), and the temporary sandbags.
